instruction: Independently check each original natural-language question, formula solution, rubric and cited local support. Inspect the exact local declaration and its hypotheses. Treat authored support/boundary claims as claims to audit. Explain which parts the cited Lean does not prove. No earlier reviewer verdict is supplied. There is no equivalent Lean task and no anonymous Lean reconstruction to certify; do not create one. Return accept, repair-required or reject with mathematical, support and scoring evidence, explicit source-assumption differences and unresolved repair requests. Do not edit the catalog or prior reports. This is editorial review, not theorem publication or a measured benchmark run.

assumptions: Let \(P,Q\) be two probability laws on \(\Omega=\{0,1\}^{\mathbb N}\) with the product sigma algebra. Let \(H_t=(X_1,\dots,X_t)\) and \(\mathcal F_t=\sigma(H_t)\). The finite marginals come from normalized conditional tables \(p_t(x\mid h)\), \(q_t(x\mid h)\) for \(X_{t+1}\) at each history \(h\) of length \(t\). At every \(P\)-positive history, \(q_t(x\mid h)=0\) if \(p_t(x\mid h)=0\).

The two laws use the same stopping rule \(\tau\), a stopping time of the canonical histories, with a common deterministic dummy bit after stopping. Assume \(P(\tau<\infty)=1\); do not assume \(Q(\tau<\infty)=1\). Let \(W\ge0\) be measurable on the full path space, possibly \(+\infty\) on exceptional paths, with \(\mathbb E_P W^2<\infty\). Think of \(W\) as total work, including any output-dependent terminal charge.

At a \(P\)-positive history define \[\eta_t(h)=\sum_{x:p_t(x\mid h)>0}\frac{(q_t(x\mid h)-p_t(x\mid h))^2}{p_t(x\mid h)}.\] On other histories set it to zero. For the positive result assume a deterministic \(B\ge0\) with \(\sum_{t<n}\eta_t(H_t)\le B\) simultaneously for all \(n\), \(P\)-almost surely.

This is a proposed alternative cost-transfer interface, not a statement of either paper. For source comparison the linked local TV result controls output event discrepancies under an integrable local budget and a common Markov suffix. The linked query result gives first-moment work information for one actual SPHMC phase under its own input assumptions. Neither supplies a full-path likelihood-ratio or stopped-work \(L^2\) bound.
mathematical_cores.boundary: Original unpaired natural-language audit with a complete binary-path calculation. Not a general-state Lean theorem, not the Gaussian Cloud or SPHMC source argument, not a claim that their actual algorithms satisfy the new likelihood or stopped-work assumptions. The same public development family is retained; no held-out or calibrated-level claim.
mathematical_cores.difficulty_reason: Audit an unbounded-cost transfer not supplied by the source TV argument. Design the predictable compensator for the finite likelihood ratios, obtain a density on the entire stopped path sigma algebra, and refute the tempting replacement by ideal-history average budgets with an explicit bounded-second-moment family.
mathematical_cores.lean_explanation: The optional module proves eventwise conditional averaging and its common-suffix preservation, not pathwise chi-square control. The separate linked SPHMC declaration supplies actual phase query moments and expected work under its hypotheses; it is not a second moment of the total stopped query count. Neither implements the predictable-compensator, path-density extension or counterexample below. There is no aligned Lean QA.
mathematical_cores.question: Prove that the finite-prefix likelihood ratios yield a full-path density \(L=dQ/dP\) with \(\mathbb E_P L^2\le e^B\). Justify why the same stopping rule terminates \(Q\)-almost surely and show \[|\mathbb E_Q W-\mathbb E_P W|\le \sqrt{(e^B-1)\operatorname{Var}_P(W)}.\] Then audit the proposed replacement \(\sup_n\sum_{t<n}\mathbb E_P\eta_t(H_t)\le 2\): construct a two-active-call family with this averaged budget and \(\mathbb E_P W^2\le 1\), but unbounded \(\mathbb E_Q W\) across the family. Identify the additional interfaces needed before applying the positive result to the cited TV and query-work routes.

rubric.criterion: Constructs valid finite-prefix densities, checks local support and the two conditional moments, and obtains the correct uniform square bound with a predictable compensator (or an equivalent valid argument).
Identifies the full-path density by a justified convergence and cylinder-extension argument; transfers almost-sure termination and the centered variance estimate without assuming Q integrability.
Gives a valid family with bounded summed ideal-average budgets and unit-bounded ideal work second moment, but divergent implemented mean; verifies the actual conditional tables and work moments.

Distinguishes the added absolute continuity, pathwise likelihood and actual stopped-work second-moment interfaces from the source TV and single-phase expected-work results. Does not claim a transfer to either actual algorithm.

mathematical_cores.source_note: Original Samplinglib mathematical QA over two owned supporting publications: gaussian-cloud-kernel-hybrid-telescope.json (common-suffix eventwise TV) and sphmc-implemented-phase-query-work.json (single actual phase query moments/work). It probes the explicitly excluded TV-to-unbounded-cost inference by adding a different conditional likelihood hypothesis and testing a weaker substitute. The positive result and counterexample are new exposition, not quotations or attributed paper statements. Only original project Apache-2.0 material is used, and this stays in the public adaptive-hybrid-cost-boundary family.
steps: Every \(Q\)-positive finite prefix is \(P\)-positive by induction from the empty prefix and the local support condition. Set \(L_0=1\) and \(L_t=Q(H_t)/P(H_t)\) on \(P\)-positive atoms, zero elsewhere. Under \(P\), \(L_{t+1}=L_t q_t(X_{t+1}\mid H_t)/p_t(X_{t+1}\mid H_t)\); the denominator is positive on the realized transition almost surely. On each positive history atom the conditional first moment of the step ratio is \(1\), and its conditional second moment is \(1+\eta_t(H_t)\), by expanding the square and using both probability sums. Thus \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb E_P[L_{t+1}\mid\mathcal F_t]&=L_t,\\ \mathbb E_P[L_{t+1}^2\mid\mathcal F_t]&=L_t^2(1+\eta_t(H_t)).\end{aligned}\] All quantities at a fixed time are integrable on the finite positive atoms.

Set \(A_0=1\) and \(A_n=\prod_{t<n}(1+\eta_t(H_t))\). Crucially \(A_{t+1}\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and at least \(1\). Dividing the conditional square identity by this predictable quantity shows that \(L_n^2/A_n\) is a nonnegative \(P\)-martingale of mean \(1\). Since \(\log(1+x)\le x\) for \(x\ge0\), the assumed pathwise budget yields \(A_n\le e^B\) almost surely. Therefore \(\mathbb E_P L_n^2\le e^B\) for each \(n\). Replacing the random factors by their ideal-history averages would discard their dependence on the likelihood weight.

For \(m\ge n\), the first martingale identity and conditioning on \(\mathcal F_n\) give \(\mathbb E_P[L_mL_n]=\mathbb E_P L_n^2\). Hence \(\mathbb E_P (L_m-L_n)^2=\mathbb E_P L_m^2-\mathbb E_P L_n^2\). These squared norms are increasing and bounded, so the sequence is Cauchy in \(L^2(P)\). Completeness yields \(L\), nonnegative almost surely because the negative part is bounded in \(L^2\) by the distance to each nonnegative \(L_n\). Convergence also holds in \(L^1(P)\), so \(\mathbb E_P L=1\) and \(\mathbb E_P L^2\le e^B\). For a cylinder event in \(\mathcal F_n\), \(\int_E L_m\,dP=Q(E)\) for every \(m\ge n\). Passing to the limit and using uniqueness of probability measures on the generating cylinder algebra proves \(Q=L P\) on the full sigma algebra, not merely on each finite prefix.

The event \(\{\tau=\infty\}\) is measurable as the countable intersection of the events \(\{\tau>n\}\). It has \(P\)-probability zero and hence \(Q\)-probability zero. Change of measure gives \(\mathbb E_Q W=\mathbb E_P[LW]<\infty\) by Cauchy–Schwarz, with any \(P\)-null exceptional values irrelevant under both laws. Since \(\mathbb E_P(L-1)=0\), center \(W\) by its \(P\)-mean. Then \[\begin{aligned}\left|\mathbb E_Q W-\mathbb E_P W\right|&=\left|\mathbb E_P[(L-1)(W-\mathbb E_P W)]\right|\\ &\le\sqrt{(e^B-1)\operatorname{Var}_P(W)},\end{aligned}\] because \(\mathbb E_P(L-1)^2=\mathbb E_P L^2-1\). No bounded-work assumption or separate \(Q\)-termination premise has been used.

For integers \(m\ge2\) take \(p=m^{-2}\), \(q=m^{-1}\) as the first-bit probabilities of \(1\) under \(P,Q\). If the first bit is \(1\), let the second-bit law be \({\rm Ber}(p)\) under \(P\) and identically \(1\) under \(Q\); if the first bit is \(0\), use identically \(0\) for both. Stop after two bits and pad identically. Local support holds. The first budget is \((q-p)^2/[p(1-p)]=(m-1)/(m+1)\), and the second is \(m^2-1\) on the first-bit-one branch, zero otherwise. Hence the sum of ideal-history averages is \((m-1)/(m+1)+1-m^{-2}<2\); the rare branch has no uniform pathwise budget.

For \(E=\{X_1=X_2=1\}\), \(P(E)=m^{-4}\), \(Q(E)=m^{-1}\). Charge an additional terminal work \(W=m^2\mathbf 1_E\), distinct from the number of the two active calls. Then \[\mathbb E_P W=m^{-2},\qquad \mathbb E_P W^2=1,\qquad \mathbb E_Q W=m.\] The averaged budgets and ideal work second moments stay bounded but implemented expected work does not. In fact \(\mathbb E_P L_2^2\ge Q(E)^2/P(E)=m^2\); the squared likelihood has concentrated on the same rare branch that carries the large conditional error.

To transfer this argument to an actual algorithm one must identify the common stopped history space, conditional densities and absolute continuity, a genuine pathwise conditional second-moment budget, and an ideal second moment of the actual total work. The local TV comparison supplies none of these likelihood controls, and single-phase expected query work does not certify that stopped-work second moment. The alternative interface is proved here only for the stated binary path model, not established for either paper's sampler.
mathematical_cores.support_lean_source:
import AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelTotalVariation

/-!
# Mean conditional-kernel errors and finite hybrid telescopes

This module isolates the reusable probability-kernel core of Chen--Chewi--Lu--
Zhang, arXiv:2609.38710v1, Lemma 6.3.  If two conditional Markov kernels differ
eventwise by an integrable history-dependent bound, their output laws differ by
at most the mean of that bound.  A common downstream Markov kernel preserves
the same estimate, so later adaptive computation is absorbed by data
processing.  A finite real-valued telescope then adds the adjacent hybrid
errors.

The declarations do not construct the paper's dummy-filled history kernels,
identify its `δ_t` with a measurable total-variation function, or compare the
capped ideal algorithm with its uncapped version.  Those adapters remain
separate source obligations.
-/

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory Set Finset
open scoped ProbabilityTheory BigOperators

namespace AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope

/-- An integrable pointwise event bound between two Markov kernels controls the
corresponding event discrepancy after averaging over the input law.  This is
the mean-replacement step in the adaptive hybrid argument. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |(K ∘ₘ μ).real t - (L ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤ ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  intro t ht
  have hint (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      Integrable (fun x => (M x).real t) μ := by
    apply (integrable_const (1 : ℝ)).mono'
      (M.measurable_coe ht).ennreal_toReal.aestronglyMeasurable
    exact Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => by
      rw [Real.norm_eq_abs, abs_of_nonneg ENNReal.toReal_nonneg]
      exact (measureReal_le_one : (M x).real t ≤ 1)
  have happly (M : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel M] :
      (M ∘ₘ μ).real t = ∫ x, (M x).real t ∂μ := by
    change (Measure.bind μ M t).toReal = ∫ x, (M x t).toReal ∂μ
    rw [Measure.bind_apply ht M.aemeasurable]
    exact (integral_toReal (M.measurable_coe ht).aemeasurable
      (Filter.Eventually.of_forall fun x => measure_lt_top (M x) t)).symm
  rw [happly K, happly L, ← integral_sub (hint K) (hint L)]
  exact abs_integral_le_integral_abs.trans <|
    integral_mono_ae ((hint K).sub (hint L)).abs hε <|
      hbound.mono fun x hx => hx t ht

/-- The same mean replacement bound survives a common downstream Markov
kernel.  In an adjacent adaptive hybrid, the downstream kernel represents all
later calls after the one conditional rule being replaced. -/
theorem abs_real_comp_commonSuffix_sub_le_integral_eventBound
    {A B C : Type*} [MeasurableSpace A] [MeasurableSpace B] [MeasurableSpace C]
    (μ : Measure A) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
    (K L : Kernel A B) [IsMarkovKernel K] [IsMarkovKernel L]
    (S : Kernel B C) [IsMarkovKernel S]
    (ε : A → ℝ) (hε : Integrable ε μ)
    (hbound : ∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ s, MeasurableSet s →
      |(K x).real s - (L x).real s| ≤ ε x) :
    ∀ t, MeasurableSet t →
      |((S ∘ₖ K) ∘ₘ μ).real t - ((S ∘ₖ L) ∘ₘ μ).real t| ≤
        ∫ x, ε x ∂μ := by
  have hKL := abs_real_comp_sub_le_integral_eventBound μ K L ε hε hbound
  have hS := KernelTotalVariation.abs_real_comp_sub_le
    (K ∘ₘ μ) (L ∘ₘ μ) S hKL
  simpa only [← Measure.comp_assoc] using hS

/-- Finite adjacent-hybrid errors telescope.  Applying this to the output laws
of hybrids `0, ..., n` turns the one-slot bounds into their accumulated error.
The result is deliberately stated for real sequences so it does not invent a
second total-variation definition. -/
theorem abs_sub_zero_le_sum_range_of_adjacent
    (a δ : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hstep : ∀ i < n, |a (i + 1) - a i| ≤ δ i) :
    |a n - a 0| ≤ ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp
  | succ n ih =>
      calc
        |a (n + 1) - a 0| ≤ |a (n + 1) - a n| + |a n - a 0| := by
          exact abs_sub_le _ _ _
        _ ≤ δ n + ∑ i ∈ range n, δ i :=
          add_le_add (hstep n (Nat.lt_succ_self n))
            (ih fun i hi => hstep i (hi.trans (Nat.lt_succ_self n)))
        _ = ∑ i ∈ range (n + 1), δ i := by
          rw [sum_range_succ, add_comm]

end AutoSamplingTheory.TechnicalLemmas.Probability.KernelHybridTelescope
